title: Ehlers Decycler (DECYCLER)
summary: Removes the cycles shorter than a cutoff period from price, leaving a trend line with very little lag.
descriptionHtml:
The Decycler subtracts a high-pass filter from price. A two-pole high-pass filter keeps only the swings shorter than the cutoff Period and blocks the slower movement. Taking that output away from price leaves the slower part: the trend, with the short cycles removed.

The filter works on the second difference of price, the change in the bar-to-bar change, and feeds back its own previous two values. Its coefficients come from the cutoff period through a cosine and a sine of 0.707 * 2 * pi / Period. The filter is held at zero for the first two bars, and a price before the first bar is read as zero.
howToReadHtml:
Read the Decycler as a trend line that lags far less than a moving average of a similar length. Price above a rising Decycler describes an uptrend and price below a falling one a downtrend, and a change in its slope marks a change in the trend.

The cutoff period sets what counts as noise: a cycle shorter than it is removed, a longer one passes through into the line. A short period leaves a line close to price; a long one gives a smoother line that turns later. Over the first stretch of bars the filter is still settling.

settings.label: Period
settings.html: The cutoff period of the high-pass filter. Swings shorter than this are removed; longer values give a smoother trend line.

settings.label: Source
settings.html: The price series that is filtered, the close by default.

faq.q: Why does it lag less than a moving average?
faq.html: Instead of averaging a window of bars, it subtracts a high-pass filter from price. Only the swings shorter than the cutoff are removed, so the slower movement of price passes through almost unchanged.

faq.q: What does the period mean here?
faq.html: It is the cycle length in bars at which the filter starts to remove movement. Shorter cycles are taken out, longer ones remain in the line.

related.title: Double Exponential Moving Average (DEMA)
related.summary: Two chained exponential averages combined as twice the first minus the second, which removes much of the lag of a single EMA.

related.title: Cubic Regression Moving Average (CRMA)
related.summary: Fits a cubic curve to the lookback window by least squares and plots the fitted value at the newest bar.

related.title: Deviation-Scaled Moving Average (DSMA)
related.summary: An adaptive average that speeds up when its tracking error is large against its recent size and slows down when it is small.
